notes: Net map (four parallel branches hung between two rails): n1 = top rail, one unbroken pencil line from the left corner at (30,139) to the right corner at (425,141), verified pixel-continuous end to end; it carries the top of Resistor 5 (10 ohm), the top of I-DC 0 (5A), the top of Resistor 3 (4 ohm) and the (+) terminal of V-DC 6 (10V). 0 = bottom rail, the slightly down-slanted line from (36,341) to (428,339); it carries the bottom plate of Capacitor 1, the bottom of I-DC 0, the bottom of Inductor 4, the bottom of V-DC 6 and GND 2, whose stem drops from the rail at x~176 into the ground symbol at y~365 - so the whole rail is net '0'. n2 = right-branch mid node, bottom of Resistor 3 down the x~325 link to the top of Inductor 4. n3 = left-branch mid node, bottom of Resistor 5 down the x~33 link to the top plate of Capacitor 1 (plates at y=228 and y=241, the lead enters the top plate at x=32 and leaves the bottom plate at x=32, so R5 and C1 are in series in the left branch, not in parallel - the plates are just drawn much wider than the wire). Judgment calls: (a) no crossings, dots or hops exist in this drawing; every branch meets the rails at a plain T; (b) Capacitor 1's wide left-overhanging plates initially look like a separate horizontal element, but the branch wire visibly enters the top plate and exits the bottom plate at the same x, so it is a series capacitor; (c) V-DC 6 is drawn with '+' above '-' inside the circle, so index 0 = top (+) on n1 and index 1 = bottom on the ground rail; I-DC 0's arrow points up and its index 0 is the top terminal; (d) all other 2-terminal parts are indexed top-then-bottom as drawn - order affects no metric; (e) the bootstrap left Capacitor 1 and V-DC 6 fully null and had Resistor 5's bottom null; those resolve to n3/0 and n1/0 respectively.
